muse_spark_1.3/001: The strategy is center control with exact Havannah win detection and shallow minimax. Hex adjacency is column staggered, odd columns up biased as in the example, auto calibrated by counting degree-3 corners. Corners are degree-3 cells, border is degree <6, edges are the 6 components of border minus corners. Bridge is one group touching 2 corners, fork is one group touching 3 distinct edges, ring is enclosure detected by flooding non-player cells from the border - any unreached valid cell is enclosed. Policy first takes a winning move, then blocks a single opponent winning move, otherwise searches candidates within 2 hex steps of stones. Evaluation rewards large connected groups, groups touching 1-2 edges, groups touching corners and central stones. 1-ply ordering plus 2-ply minimax over top moves picks double threats while staying in time, always falling back to a legal empty cell.
muse_spark_1.3/002: The strategy is central control with exact Havannah win detection and short tactical search. Neighbours use odd-q offset, board geometry (border, 6 degree-3 corners, 6 edges) is auto-derived from `valid_mask`. Wins are bridge (2 corners in one group), fork (3 edges in one group) and ring (enclosed non-player component whose neighbouring stones are connected). Each move first takes an immediate winning move, then blocks opponent immediate wins, then searches for double-threats that create 2+ winning follow-ups and blocks opponent double-threats. Otherwise a 1-ply virtual-connection search is used: 0-1 BFS from own stones (0 through own, 1 through empty, blocked through opponent) gives distance to every edge/corner, fork cost is sum of 3 smallest edge distances, bridge cost sum of 2 smallest corner distances, overall cost is the minimum. Move value is opponent cost minus own cost after the move, preferring centre and adjacency. All checks are restricted to frontier cells and top heuristics to stay well under 1s, with a safe legal fallback.
muse_spark_1.3/003: The strategy is central connected play with exact tactical win/block search. Bridges and forks are detected by connectivity to board borders, corners and edges inferred from the mask geometry, rings by enclosure of the complement. Immediate wins are taken, immediate losses blocked, two-step double threats are created when possible, otherwise a heuristic favouring large connected groups touching many different edges/corners, centrality and adjacency to both sides is used with candidate pruning to stay well under time.
muse_spark_1.3/004: The strategy is central control with connectivity for fork/bridge and enclosure detection for rings. Topology is auto-detected from the mask using column-offset hex adjacency, corners are degree-3 cells and edges are angular arcs between them. Wins are tested by component edge/corner touches and by flood-fill from the border for rings. The policy takes immediate wins, blocks immediate losses, then scores moves by adjacency, merging, centrality and static distance to uncovered edges/corners and runs a depth-2 minimax over the top candidates under a time guard, always falling back to a legal empty cell.
muse_spark_1.3/005: The strategy is central control with exact Havannah win detection and forced mate search. Neighbours use column parity, even-q offset, which matches the example adjacency. Cube coordinates centre the board to label the 6 corners and 6 edges. Bridge is 2 corners in one component, fork is 3 edges in one component, ring is a cycle in the stone graph. A new stone can only win by merging its neighbouring components, so immediate wins are tested in O(1) after one DSU. The policy wins if possible, blocks opponent wins, then searches for a move that creates two winning replies, then blocks opponent double-threat creation, otherwise picks the best heuristic move favouring merging components, edge/corner progress, opponent blocking, clustering for rings and centre to outward expansion.
